## Check the distinctions

A letter “é” is displayed on screen. Which statement correctly distinguishes the representation layers?

1. A character is an abstract text unit; a Unicode code point identifies an element of the code space; UTF-8 encodes code points as bytes.
2. A character is always one byte; a code point is the token; UTF-8 is the model's vocabulary.
3. A code point and a UTF-8 byte are two names for the same thing.

<details>
<summary>Show the answer and reasoning</summary>

The first statement is correct. A perceived character may be represented by one or more code points; each code point is then encoded as a sequence of one to four UTF-8 bytes. Normalization can also map distinct sequences to the same normalized form. Neither code points nor bytes are, by themselves, the tokens or IDs of a particular tokenizer.

</details>
